title: Grammar: Passive voice, impersonal on and the gerund
subtitle: B1 · Unit 9: B1 · Talk about how things are done and what you experienced

steps.title: Passive voice, impersonal on and the gerund
steps.body: Use the passive when the result or process matters more than the person doing it: Les places sont attribuées par tirage. Use on for a natural general account when the actor is not named: On remet un reçu. The gerund is en + present participle and normally keeps the same subject as the main clause: En remplissant le formulaire, vous confirmez votre présence. Do not use it when another person is doing the second action. Prefer an active sentence when it is clearer to say who did the action.

steps.title: Passive voice, impersonal on and the gerund
rows: Les badges ont été distribués à l'entrée.
Badges were handed out at the entrance.
On remet un reçu après l'inscription.
A receipt is given after registration.
En participant, j'ai rencontré des voisins.
By taking part, I met neighbours.

options: Les bénévoles ont distribué les badges.
Les badges ont été distribués à l'entrée.
steps.explain: The subject receives the action: les badges ont été distribués.

steps.prompt: Which sentence uses on for a general procedure?
options: Le reçu a été remis hier.
On remet un reçu après l'inscription.
Nous avons remis le reçu à Nadia.
steps.explain: The sentence describes a general process without naming the actor.

steps.prompt: When is a gerund subject clear?
options: The same subject does both actions
The main clause has no verb
A different person does each action
steps.explain: The gerund normally shares the subject of the main clause.
